// Code generated by riddim. DO NOT EDIT.

// Package rt is the Riddim runtime: Option, Result, Map, list helpers and
// the capabilities. It is the same for every program, so Go's build cache
// compiles it once and reuses it across programs and edits. Generated code
// names it rt, a name Riddim code cannot take for itself.
package rt

import (
	"cmp"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"math"
	"os"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// Option is Riddim's Option<T>: Some(Value) when IsSome is set, else None.
type Option[T any] struct {
	IsSome bool
	Value  T
}

// Some makes Some(v).
func Some[T any](v T) Option[T] { return Option[T]{IsSome: true, Value: v} }

// None makes None.
func None[T any]() Option[T] { return Option[T]{} }

// Result is Riddim's Result<T, E>: Ok(Value) when IsOk is set, else Err(Err).
type Result[T, E any] struct {
	IsOk  bool
	Value T
	Err   E
}

// Ok makes Ok(v).
func Ok[T, E any](v T) Result[T, E] { return Result[T, E]{IsOk: true, Value: v} }

// Err makes Err(e).
func Err[T, E any](e E) Result[T, E] { return Result[T, E]{Err: e} }

// IsVariant reports whether an enum value is the variant V.
func IsVariant[V any](x any) bool {
	_, ok := x.(V)
	return ok
}

// Lists are immutable: no helper changes a slice it is given, and ListPush
// always copies, so two lists never share storage that one of them changes.

func ListGet[T any](xs []T, i int) Option[T] {
	if i < 0 || i >= len(xs) {
		return None[T]()
	}
	return Some(xs[i])
}

func ListPush[T any](xs []T, x T) []T {
	return append(xs[:len(xs):len(xs)], x)
}

func ListMap[T, U any](xs []T, f func(T) U) []U {
	out := make([]U, len(xs))
	for i, x := range xs {
		out[i] = f(x)
	}
	return out
}

func ListFilter[T any](xs []T, f func(T) bool) []T {
	out := make([]T, 0, len(xs))
	for _, x := range xs {
		if f(x) {
			out = append(out, x)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func ListFold[T, U any](xs []T, acc U, f func(U, T) U) U {
	for _, x := range xs {
		acc = f(acc, x)
	}
	return acc
}

func ListFirst[T any](xs []T) Option[T] { return ListGet(xs, 0) }

func ListLast[T any](xs []T) Option[T] { return ListGet(xs, len(xs)-1) }

// ListSet is List.set: a copy with element i replaced. It panics out of
// range, as xs[i] does.
func ListSet[T any](xs []T, i int, x T) []T {
	out := slices.Clone(xs)
	out[i] = x
	return out
}

func ListConcat[T any](xs, ys []T) []T {
	return append(xs[:len(xs):len(xs)], ys...)
}

// ListSlice is List.slice: the elements from start up to, not including,
// end. It checks the bounds against the length: a list's capacity may be
// larger.
func ListSlice[T any](xs []T, start, end int) []T {
	if start < 0 || end < start || end > len(xs) {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("slice(%d, %d) is out of range for a list of length %d", start, end, len(xs)))
	}
	return xs[start:end:end]
}

func ListReverse[T any](xs []T) []T {
	out := slices.Clone(xs)
	slices.Reverse(out)
	return out
}

func ListAny[T any](xs []T, f func(T) bool) bool {
	for _, x := range xs {
		if f(x) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func ListAll[T any](xs []T, f func(T) bool) bool {
	for _, x := range xs {
		if !f(x) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func ListFind[T any](xs []T, f func(T) bool) Option[T] {
	for _, x := range xs {
		if f(x) {
			return Some(x)
		}
	}
	return None[T]()
}

func ListContains[T comparable](xs []T, x T) bool { return slices.Contains(xs, x) }

func ListIndexOf[T comparable](xs []T, x T) Option[int] {
	if i := slices.Index(xs, x); i >= 0 {
		return Some(i)
	}
	return None[int]()
}

// ListSort is List.sort: a sorted copy, with any NaN first.
func ListSort[T cmp.Ordered](xs []T) []T {
	out := slices.Clone(xs)
	slices.Sort(out)
	return out
}

// ListMin is List.min. Like Go's min, it gives NaN if a Float is NaN.
func ListMin[T cmp.Ordered](xs []T) Option[T] {
	if len(xs) == 0 {
		return None[T]()
	}
	m := xs[0]
	for _, x := range xs[1:] {
		m = min(m, x)
	}
	return Some(m)
}

func ListMax[T cmp.Ordered](xs []T) Option[T] {
	if len(xs) == 0 {
		return None[T]()
	}
	m := xs[0]
	for _, x := range xs[1:] {
		m = max(m, x)
	}
	return Some(m)
}

func ListSum[T int | float64](xs []T) T {
	var sum T
	for _, x := range xs {
		sum += x
	}
	return sum
}

// IntAbs is Int.abs. It wraps for the smallest Int, whose negation does not
// fit.
func IntAbs(n int) int {
	if n < 0 {
		return -n
	}
	return n
}

func StringFind(s, sub string) Option[int] {
	if i := strings.Index(s, sub); i >= 0 {
		return Some(i)
	}
	return None[int]()
}

// StringLines is String.lines: the lines without their "\n" or "\r\n". A
// final line ending does not add an empty line.
func StringLines(s string) []string {
	lines := strings.Split(s, "\n")
	if lines[len(lines)-1] == "" {
		lines = lines[:len(lines)-1]
	}
	for i, l := range lines {
		lines[i] = strings.TrimSuffix(l, "\r")
	}
	return lines
}

// StringSlice is String.slice: the bytes from start up to, not including,
// end. It panics out of range and off a character boundary.
func StringSlice(s string, start, end int) string {
	if start < 0 || end < start || end > len(s) {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("slice(%d, %d) is out of range for a string of %d bytes", start, end, len(s)))
	}
	if start < len(s) && !utf8.RuneStart(s[start]) || end < len(s) && !utf8.RuneStart(s[end]) {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("slice(%d, %d) is not on a character boundary", start, end))
	}
	return s[start:end]
}

// Map is Riddim's Map<K, V>: immutable, iterated in insertion order. keys
// and vals hold the entries in order, and index maps each key to its place.
// No helper changes a Map it is given: insert and remove make a new one, so
// two maps never share storage that one of them changes.
type Map[K comparable, V any] struct {
	Keys  []K
	Vals  []V
	Index map[K]int
}

func MapGet[K comparable, V any](m Map[K, V], k K) Option[V] {
	if i, ok := m.Index[k]; ok {
		return Some(m.Vals[i])
	}
	return None[V]()
}

func MapContainsKey[K comparable, V any](m Map[K, V], k K) bool {
	_, ok := m.Index[k]
	return ok
}

// MapInsert adds k last, or gives a key that is already there its new value
// in its place.
func MapInsert[K comparable, V any](m Map[K, V], k K, v V) Map[K, V] {
	if i, ok := m.Index[k]; ok {
		vals := slices.Clone(m.Vals)
		vals[i] = v
		return Map[K, V]{Keys: m.Keys, Vals: vals, Index: m.Index}
	}
	index := make(map[K]int, len(m.Keys)+1)
	for key, i := range m.Index {
		index[key] = i
	}
	index[k] = len(m.Keys)
	return Map[K, V]{Keys: ListPush(m.Keys, k), Vals: ListPush(m.Vals, v), Index: index}
}

func MapRemove[K comparable, V any](m Map[K, V], k K) Map[K, V] {
	at, ok := m.Index[k]
	if !ok {
		return m
	}
	out := Map[K, V]{Index: make(map[K]int, len(m.Keys)-1)}
	for i, key := range m.Keys {
		if i != at {
			out.Index[key] = len(out.Keys)
			out.Keys = append(out.Keys, key)
			out.Vals = append(out.Vals, m.Vals[i])
		}
	}
	return out
}

func OptionUnwrapOr[T any](o Option[T], d T) T {
	if o.IsSome {
		return o.Value
	}
	return d
}

func OptionMap[T, U any](o Option[T], f func(T) U) Option[U] {
	if o.IsSome {
		return Some(f(o.Value))
	}
	return None[U]()
}

func OptionAndThen[T, U any](o Option[T], f func(T) Option[U]) Option[U] {
	if o.IsSome {
		return f(o.Value)
	}
	return None[U]()
}

func OptionOkOr[T, E any](o Option[T], e E) Result[T, E] {
	if o.IsSome {
		return Ok[T, E](o.Value)
	}
	return Err[T](e)
}

func OptionUnwrap[T any](o Option[T]) T {
	if !o.IsSome {
		panic("called unwrap() on None")
	}
	return o.Value
}

func OptionExpect[T any](o Option[T], msg string) T {
	if !o.IsSome {
		panic(msg)
	}
	return o.Value
}

func ResultUnwrapOr[T, E any](r Result[T, E], d T) T {
	if r.IsOk {
		return r.Value
	}
	return d
}

func ResultMap[T, E, U any](r Result[T, E], f func(T) U) Result[U, E] {
	if r.IsOk {
		return Ok[U, E](f(r.Value))
	}
	return Err[U](r.Err)
}

func ResultMapErr[T, E, F any](r Result[T, E], f func(E) F) Result[T, F] {
	if r.IsOk {
		return Ok[T, F](r.Value)
	}
	return Err[T](f(r.Err))
}

func ResultAndThen[T, E, U any](r Result[T, E], f func(T) Result[U, E]) Result[U, E] {
	if r.IsOk {
		return f(r.Value)
	}
	return Err[U](r.Err)
}

func ResultOk[T, E any](r Result[T, E]) Option[T] {
	if r.IsOk {
		return Some(r.Value)
	}
	return None[T]()
}

func ResultUnwrap[T, E any](r Result[T, E]) T {
	if !r.IsOk {
		panic("called unwrap() on Err: " + describeValue(r.Err))
	}
	return r.Value
}

func ResultExpect[T, E any](r Result[T, E], msg string) T {
	if !r.IsOk {
		panic(msg + ": " + describeValue(r.Err))
	}
	return r.Value
}

func describeValue(v any) string {
	switch v := v.(type) {
	case error:
		return v.Error()
	case string:
		return v
	}
	return fmt.Sprint(v)
}

// ParseInt is String.parse_int: base 10, an optional sign, no spaces.
func ParseInt(s string) Result[int, error] {
	n, err := strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 64)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, strconv.ErrRange) {
			return Err[int](fmt.Errorf("cannot parse %q as Int: out of range", s))
		}
		return Err[int](fmt.Errorf("cannot parse %q as Int", s))
	}
	return Ok[int, error](int(n))
}

// FloatToInt is `f as Int`: it truncates toward zero and saturates at the
// ends of Int; NaN gives 0. Go's int(f) is implementation-dependent there.
func FloatToInt(f float64) int {
	switch {
	case math.IsNaN(f):
		return 0
	case f >= 1<<63:
		return math.MaxInt64
	case f <= -(1 << 63):
		return math.MinInt64
	}
	return int(f)
}

// FloatToByte is `f as Byte`: it truncates toward zero and saturates at 0 and
// 255; NaN gives 0.
func FloatToByte(f float64) byte {
	switch {
	case math.IsNaN(f) || f <= 0:
		return 0
	case f >= 255:
		return 255
	}
	return byte(f)
}

// ParseFloat is String.parse_float, as Go's strconv.ParseFloat: it also
// reads "Inf" and "NaN".
func ParseFloat(s string) Result[float64, error] {
	f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, strconv.ErrRange) {
			return Err[float64](fmt.Errorf("cannot parse %q as Float: out of range", s))
		}
		return Err[float64](fmt.Errorf("cannot parse %q as Float", s))
	}
	return Ok[float64, error](f)
}

// ListCopy copies a list on its way to or from Go, so that Go code never
// holds a Riddim list's storage.
func ListCopy[T any](xs []T) []T { return slices.Clone(xs) }

// GoResult turns a Go function's results (v, err) into a Result.
func GoResult[T any](v T, err error) Result[T, error] {
	if err != nil {
		return Err[T](err)
	}
	return Ok[T, error](v)
}

// GoError turns a Go function's error result into a Result<(), Error>.
func GoError(err error) Result[struct{}, error] {
	if err != nil {
		return Err[struct{}](err)
	}
	return Ok[struct{}, error](struct{}{})
}

// Out is the Out capability: a stream to print to.
type Out struct{ w *os.File }

func (o Out) Print(s string)   { o.w.WriteString(s) }
func (o Out) Println(s string) { o.w.WriteString(s + "\n") }

// Env is the Env capability: the program's environment and arguments.
type Env struct{}

// get is Env.get: the value of an environment variable, or None when it is
// not set.
func (Env) Get(name string) Option[string] {
	if v, ok := os.LookupEnv(name); ok {
		return Some(v)
	}
	return None[string]()
}

// args is Env.args: the program's arguments, without its name.
func (Env) Args() []string { return slices.Clone(os.Args[1:]) }

// Fs is the Fs capability: the file system. Relative paths are relative to
// the directory the program runs in.
type Fs struct{}

// read is Fs.read: the text of a file, which must be UTF-8.
func (Fs) Read(path string) Result[string, error] {
	b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return Err[string](fsError("read", path, err))
	}
	if !utf8.Valid(b) {
		return Err[string](fmt.Errorf("cannot read %s: it is not UTF-8 text", path))
	}
	return Ok[string, error](string(b))
}

// write is Fs.write: it creates a file, or replaces what it holds, with
// text.
func (Fs) Write(path, text string) Result[struct{}, error] {
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(text), 0o644); err != nil {
		return Err[struct{}](fsError("write", path, err))
	}
	return Ok[struct{}, error](struct{}{})
}

// exists is Fs.exists: whether there is a file or a directory at path.
func (Fs) Exists(path string) bool {
	_, err := os.Stat(path)
	return err == nil
}

// list is Fs.list: the names in a directory, sorted.
func (Fs) List(dir string) Result[[]string, error] {
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return Err[[]string](fsError("list", dir, err))
	}
	names := make([]string, len(entries))
	for i, e := range entries {
		names[i] = e.Name()
	}
	return Ok[[]string, error](names)
}

// fsError describes a failed file operation the same way on every system,
// as in "cannot read notes.txt: no such file or directory".
func fsError(op, path string, err error) error {
	reason := err.Error()
	var pe *fs.PathError
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
		reason = "no such file or directory"
	case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrPermission):
		reason = "permission denied"
	case errors.As(err, &pe):
		reason = pe.Err.Error()
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("cannot %s %s: %s", op, path, reason)
}

// Clock is the Clock capability: the time.
type Clock struct{}

// now_ms is Clock.now_ms: Unix time in milliseconds.
func (Clock) NowMs() int { return int(time.Now().UnixMilli()) }

// Sys is the root capability, handed to main: standard output and error,
// the environment, the file system and the clock.
type Sys struct {
	Out   Out
	Err   Out
	Env   Env
	Fs    Fs
	Clock Clock
}

// NewSys makes the Sys that main receives.
func NewSys() Sys { return Sys{Out: Out{os.Stdout}, Err: Out{os.Stderr}} }

// ExitWithError ends the program when main returns an Err.
func ExitWithError(err error) {
	os.Stderr.WriteString("error: " + err.Error() + "\n")
	os.Exit(1)
}
